name: fizmo
why: A Z-Machine interpreter for classic text adventures; a window into the old virtual machine that ran Infocom games.

brief.what_it_is: Fizmo is a Z-Machine interpreter written in plain C. It runs story files for Z-Machine versions 1 to 5, 7 and 8 (version 6 is not listed), so you can play interactive fiction, including Infocom games and games made with the Inform compiler, in a terminal or in a window. It ships with ncurses, SDL2 and console frontends (the brew executables are fizmo-console, fizmo-ncursesw and fizmo-sdl2). It is also a development library for building your own interactive fiction front end in C, C++ or Objective-C.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no explicit mission statement. It says the project provides an interpreter library plus frontends so people can play classic interactive fiction on a terminal, and so developers can write their own front ends.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage does not explain the internals. It says the library is plain C, that the ncurses, SDL2 and console frontends sit on top of it, and that the GLK interface was mostly written by Andrew Plotkin. Version 0.8 added the SDL2 interface with proportional font display, sub-pixel rendering and Hi-DPI support.
brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no install instructions, accounts or runtime requirements beyond the brew formula. The formula's executables are fizmo-console, fizmo-ncursesw and fizmo-sdl2. The SDL2 frontend presumably needs SDL2 libraries, but I did not confirm that. I did not read a README or docs, so anything beyond the homepage is unverified.
brief.standout: The homepage notes that Andrew Plotkin built iOS-fizmo on top of the project for the Hadean Lands Kickstarter, so authors can package games for the Apple App Store. The Dreamhold, Shade and Heliopause were released that way for iPhone and iPad, and Jason McIntosh adapted The Warbler's Nest. So it is both a desktop terminal player and the base of mobile releases of interactive fiction.
brief.status: quiet: the stable release is 0.8.5, dated September 10, 2017, and the homepage describes development as running from 2005 to 2017 with no later version mentioned. I found no changelog, commit history or newer release on the page, so this is inferred from the homepage alone.
brief.caveats: I read only the homepage. It contains no command lines, no README and no docs links, so I could not verify build steps or options. The homepage does not say what license applies. Version 6 of the Z-Machine is not listed as supported. The last release is from 2017, so newer platform or library changes may not be handled.
quotes: Fizmo provides a Z-Machine interpreter development library in plain C
fizmo was written from 2005 to 2017 by Christoph Ender.
